t: Section 2102 of the Water Resources Reform and Development Act of 2014 (Public Law 113–121; 128 Stat. 1273) is amended by adding at the end the following:“(d) Guidance.—Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of the Water Resources Development Act of 2016, the Secretary shall publish on the website of the Corps of Engineers guidance on the implementation of this section and the amendments made by this section.”.

fable.w: The section only directs the Secretary to post implementation guidance on the Corps of Engineers website, which is one-way disclosure by a federal official. It is tempting to treat publishing guidance as rulemaking, but the text requires no regulation, comment period, hearing, or consultation with any party outside the federal government. No outside party is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary shall publish on the website of the Corps of Engineers guidance on the implementation of this section and the amendments made by this section

opus.w: This section only requires the Secretary to post implementation guidance on the Corps of Engineers website. It is tempting to treat this like the regulation authority in Example 6. But guidance is not rulemaking, and the section has no comment period, hearing, or consultation with anyone outside the federal government. Publishing a finished document is a one-way communication, and outsiders get no role in the decision.
opus.s: the Secretary shall publish on the website of the Corps of Engineers guidance on the implementation of this section and the amendments made by this section.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary to publish guidance on a website. This is a one-way dissemination of information by the federal government to the public. It does not require the government to consult, coordinate with, or receive input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary shall publish on the website of the Corps of Engineers guidance on the implementation of this section and the amendments made by this section
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that publishing guidance on a website constitutes a form of public participation or transparency. However, the definition of participation requires that the government *consult* or *coordinate* with people outside the government *before* making a decision, or that there is a mechanism for outside input (like a comment period). Merely publishing information or guidance is a one-way communication from the government to the public and does not involve the public in the decision-making process itself. There is no requirement for public comment, hearing, or advisory input in this text.
